extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal policymakers, research administrators, and scientific community leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for creating and operating a national research funding organization and for federal support of scientific research (pure, background, applied), with principles for university support, budgeting, and protection of academic freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augment quality as well as quantity of research
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal program of research support should seek to augment both the quality and the quantity of scientific research rather than merely increasing funding amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete proposals should aim to improve research quality; mere existence of a program is not enough—ill-devised distributions can harm science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ill-devised distribution of Federal funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal research funds must be distributed in a manner that aids, not hinders, the growth of science; poor allocation can be detrimental despite having a program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sound administrative practice is required to prevent harmful outcomes from funding misallocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not create an all-seeing centralized planning board
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization established should not attempt to guide in detail the normal growth processes of science or play the role of an all-powerful planning board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid top-down detailed direction; respect the organic and unpredictable development of scientific inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator composition and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups administering research assistance must be composed of persons of the highest integrity, ability, and experience, with a thorough understanding of scientific problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff the program with the ablest personnel obtainable to ensure wise, nonpolitical stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and statutory creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Best solution is an independent government body, created by Congress, free from hampering restrictions and empowered to give sustained, far-sighted assistance with assurance of continuing support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal creation and statutory independence are important to avoid political interference and ensure continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary function of a National Research Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation's function should be promotion of scientific research and the applications of research to enhance national security and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center responsibility for research assistance in a single organization with this explicit mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize distinct categories of research
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific research should be categorized as (1) pure research, (2) background research, and (3) applied research and development; each category requires different institutional arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boundaries are fuzzy but typical instances are recognizable; policy should account for different needs and appropriate institutional settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for pure research (definition and principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure research is research without specific practical ends; it yields general knowledge and understanding and often unpredictable discoveries that benefit the public domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pure research requires freedom of mind, resists direction from above, and deserves special protection and assured support because applied work tends to crowd it out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special circumstances needed for pure research
rubrics_metrics.description: Because pure science is unpredictable and benefits from varied investigative paths, it needs special circumstances: freedom, intellectual independence, and sometimes cooperative efforts with shared expensive equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should preserve freedom and provide appropriate shared capital equipment and support for cooperative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background research suitability for government
rubrics_metrics.description: Background research (maps, standards, constants, species descriptions, etc.) has clear objectives and is well-suited to large coordinated programs, often best centralized in Federal laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results should be promptly published and made systematically available; federal centralization carries advantages because few private organizations can do this work at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applied research and development characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Applied research and development has often definite objectives, organized efforts, and practical/commercial value; heavy expenses are usually borne by private organizations expecting returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where private incentives fail (e.g., small/dispersed producing units), government support (as in agriculture) may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against applied work crowding out pure research
rubrics_metrics.description: Under pressure for immediate results, applied research tends to drive out pure research unless deliberate policies guard against this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National policy must specially protect pure research and assure its support to maintain long-term scientific progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain adequate national research volume and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy objectives should include achieving an adequate total volume of research and maintaining a proper proportion between pure and applied research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trends show industry contributes most funds; generous support to universities is essential to sustain pure research proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide for continuous and steady expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: A far-sighted national research policy should maintain continuous, steady expansion of research activities to avoid idle talent and retarded progress during economic downturns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In postwar transitions or recessions, government expenditure may need to increase to offset private reductions; a national foundation should, where consistent with policy, increase grants in depressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities as appropriate research environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities are appropriate for research because they combine responsibility for preserving past knowledge, educating students, and contributing to new knowledge, offering colleagueship and academic freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long struggle for academic freedom and group solidarity are essential for development of new knowledge, which can challenge prevailing beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of aid: direct financial support preserving academic freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Government aid to universities should be principally direct financial support provided under conditions that do not endanger academic freedom and the investigator's personal independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect aid (high-quality govt labs, libraries) is helpful, but direct support must avoid controls that compromise freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against control of science by industry or government
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on industrial support risks distorting university research toward short-range problems and may decrease scientific freedom; safeguards are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperative research with industry can be beneficial if proper safeguards are maintained to prevent undue commercial control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand sources of financial support for universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities need new sources of financial support to keep pace with economic growth and to attract and retain able researchers, given pressures on endowments and public appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rising cost of living and relatively frozen professorial earnings threaten recruitment; national policy should address these financial incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in capital facilities and convert wartime plant
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial expenditures for capital facilities are required; some wartime plant/equipment may be convertible to peacetime uses but additional investment will be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New construction for research can be among the most productive public and private investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate supplementary operating costs for research
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities must supply adequate direct operating costs (apparatus, materials, technical assistance) relative to salaries; prewar university spending typically ranged 10–40 cents per salary dollar, while industry often spent much more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice in industry ranges from $0.40 to $3 per salary dollar; universities should take steps to bring supplementary expenditures more in line with efficient research practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address training, reconversion, and retention of scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy must remedy wartime cessation of training, provide re-education and readjustment for returning scientists, and maintain university competitiveness to retain trained personnel against industrial offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid measures (e.g., excessive teaching loads) that encourage transfer to industry; in short run consider makeshifts (accelerated programs, transfers) but long-term solution is training more scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient laboratory assistance and support staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities must ensure adequate laboratory assistance, materials, apparatus, clerical and manual aid for research staff so that highly paid scientists are not used for shop or routine work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current university practice underfunds these supports; remedying this is essential for productive research.
